newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: James Baker to hold talks in London on W. Sahara.
newsitem.headline: James Baker to hold talks in London on W. Sahara.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, now serving as U.N. special envoy for Western Sahara, will hold talks in London next week with the parties involved in the dispute over the North African territory, U.N. sources said on Wednesday.

Representatives of Morocco, which controls most of the former Spanish colony, and of the Algerian-backed Polisario Front, which seeks independence for Western Sahara, have been invited to the talks, scheduled for June 11 and 12, the sources said.
Envoys from Algeria and Mauritania, both closely concerned with the issue, have also been invited. Baker is expected to hold separate meetings with each of the parties.
The United Nations has been trying for years to organise a referendum, originally set for January 1992, to decide whether Western Sahara should be incorporated into Morocco or become independent.
But the referendum, called for under a U.N. peace plan, has been repeatedly postponed because of a disagreement between the two sides over who should be eligible to vote.

Baker, who made an exploratory visit to the region in April, has the task of advising Secretary-General Kofi Annan whether the U.N. plan can still be implemented in its present form, whether adjustments acceptable to the two sides might be possible or whether other ways of resolving the conflict could be found.
He had been expected to pay a return visit to the region this month before making substantive recommendations to Annan.
It was not clear whether the London talks, for which the British Foreign Office is arranging facilities, are intended as a substitute for that trip or as a preliminary to such a visit.
The Security Council last month renewed until September 30 the mandate of a 230-member U.N. observer force called the U.N. Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO).
It has been monitoring a September 1991 ceasefire that halted a brushfire war between Morocco and Polisario dating back to Spain's withdrawal from Western Sahara in 1976.
